tldr: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Sol on Sep 29, pitching near-Astra intelligence for coding and computer use at one-fifth of Astra's API token prices. On Oct 9 Asana reported its browser agent 76x cheaper and 5x faster in tests.
whats_new: A second tech-insider.org post now puts the reported Codex CLI default switch to GPT-6.1 Sol at 77% cheaper, down from 80% two days earlier; OpenAI has not confirmed either figure.
why_it_matters: GPT-6.1 Sol lowers the price of Astra-class coding and computer-use work, so routing and cost-per-task assumptions built on Astra pricing are out of date.

status.detail: GPT-6.1 Sol has moved from launch to a customer cost claim and a reported Codex CLI default whose price cut is still unconfirmed (80%, then 77%).

beats.headline: Asana reports 76x lower model cost and 5x speed in browser-agent tests
beats.summary: Asana ran the tests with GPT-6 Astra in Codex, weeks after OpenAI's Sep 29 GPT-6.1 Sol launch.

beats.headline: Report: Codex CLI defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol; price cut restated from 80% to 77%
beats.summary: Both posts come from one outlet, tech-insider.org; OpenAI has not confirmed the default or the figure.

open_questions: Does OpenAI confirm Codex CLI's default switch to GPT-6.1 Sol, and is the cut 80% or 77%?
Does Asana's 76x cost reduction reproduce outside its browser-agent tests?
How does GPT-6.1 Sol compare with Claude Opus 5.5 on cost per completed task?
take_for_builders: Treat the Codex CLI price cut as unconfirmed: rerun your coding and computer-use evals on GPT-6.1 Sol against your Astra baseline on cost per completed task, and check OpenAI's pricing page before changing any default model.

day_captions.9bf93d58cc35db99: First customer numbers: Asana's browser agent 76x cheaper and 5x faster in tests.
day_captions.d772334624f1e023: Secondary report that Codex CLI now defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol with an 80% price cut.
day_captions.c80aaab92d6da992: Same outlet's follow-up restating the Codex CLI default with a 77% price cut instead of 80%.
